question.text:
If $x+\log _{10}\left(1+2^{x}\right)=x \log _{10} 5+\log _{10} 6,$ then
the value of $x$ is

solution.text:
We have,
$\begin{aligned} x+\log _{10}\left(1+2^{x}\right) &=x \log _{10} 5+\log _{10} 6 \\ \Rightarrow \log _{10}\left(1+2^{x}\right) &=x \log _{10} 5+\log _{10} 6-x \\ &=\log _{10} 5^{x}+\log _{10} 6-x \log _{10} 10 \\ &=\log _{10}\left(5^{x} \cdot 6\right)-\log _{10} 10^{x} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \log _{10}\left(1+2^{x}\right)=\log _{10}\left(\frac{5^{x} \cdot 6}{10^{x}}\right) \end{aligned}$
$\Rightarrow \quad 1+2^{x}=\frac{5^{x} \cdot 6}{10^{x}}=\frac{6}{2^{x}}$
$\Rightarrow \quad 2^{x}\left(1+2^{x}\right)=6$
$\Rightarrow \quad t(1+t)=6$$\quad \quad \quad\left(\operatorname{let} 2^{x}=t\right)$
$\Rightarrow \quad t^{2}+t-6=0$
$\Rightarrow \quad(t+3)(t-2)=0$
$t+3=0$
or $t-2=0$
$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow \quad t=2 \\
2^{x}=2 \Rightarrow x=1
\end{array}$
